item.title: Installing Cisco Packet Tracer on Fedora 44 Workstation Using Distrobox
item.description:
Cisco Packet Tracer is an essential tool for CCNA students and network engineers. However, Cisco officially distributes Packet Tracer as a .deb package targeting Ubuntu Linux, making native installation on RPM-based distributions like Fedora 44 Workstation tricky.

Rather than dirtying your host Fedora system with converted RPMs or extracted binaries, the cleanest solution is to isolate Cisco Packet Tracer inside an Ubuntu 24.04 Noble Numbat container via Distrobox.

This guide covers all prerequisite packages, container setup, dependency fixes, FUSE symlinks, and desktop integration for Fedora 44 Workstation Edition.

Host Prerequisites (Fedora 44 Workstation)

Before creating the container, ensure your host system has Distrobox, Podman, and the legacy FUSE kernel tools installed.

Open a terminal on your Fedora host (taylor) and install the host prerequisites:

sudo dnf install -y distrobox podman fuse
  • podman / distrobox: Provides the container runtime and seamless host integration.
  • fuse: Enables host-level FUSE mounting capabilities required by AppImage binaries inside containers.

Step 1: Create and Enter the Ubuntu Container

Create an Ubuntu 24.04 container named ubuntu-pt:

distrobox-create --name ubuntu-pt --image ubuntu:24.04

Once creation completes, enter the container shell:

distrobox-enter -n ubuntu-pt

Step 2: Install Container Base Dependencies

Inside your ubuntu-pt container shell, update package lists and install the core desktop and FUSE dependencies required by Ubuntu 24.04:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y fuse3 libglib2.0-bin desktop-file-utils shared-mime-info

Setting Up the FUSE Symlink

Cisco Packet Tracer's internal AppImage loader specifically calls fusermount, whereas Ubuntu 24.04 relies on fusermount3. Create a symbolic link inside the container to prevent AppImage mounting failures:

sudo ln -sf /usr/bin/fusermount3 /usr/bin/fusermount

Step 3: Install Cisco Packet Tracer .deb Package

Download the CiscoPacketTracer_901_Ubuntu_64bit.deb file into your host ~/Downloads directory (which is automatically mounted inside Distrobox).

Inside the container, navigate to your downloads folder and install the package:

sudo apt install ./Downloads/CiscoPacketTracer_901_Ubuntu_64bit.deb

Note

You may see a notice stating: N: Download is performed unsandboxed as root.... This is safe to ignore; it simply indicates apt fell back to root privileges to read files from your home directory.

During installation, accept the End User License Agreement (EULA). When prompted:

Would you like to run multi-user when application starts?

Select No unless you are setting up a multi-tenant shared computer lab.

Step 4: Resolve Runtime GUI and Library Dependencies

Cisco Packet Tracer depends on several dynamic libraries that are omitted from minimal container base images. Run the following command inside the container to install all missing audio, graphics, security, and XCB display dependencies:

sudo apt install -y \
    libopengl0 \
    libgl1 \
    libnss3 \
    libnspr4 \
    libxss1 \
    libasound2t64 \
    libpulse0 \
    libxcb-xinerama0 \
    libxcb-cursor0 \
    libxkbcommon-x11-0 \
    libxcb-icccm4 \
    libxcb-image0 \
    libxcb-keysyms1 \
    libxcb-randr0 \
    libxcb-render-util0 \
    libxcb-shape0 \
    libxcb-xfixes0

Summary of key dependencies:

  • libopengl0 & libgl1: Provides OpenGL rendering for the device canvas.
  • libnss3 & libnspr4: Enables internal web view components.
  • libasound2t64 & libpulse0: Handles PulseAudio client audio routing.
  • libxcb-*: Provides X11/XCB platform plugins for Qt application window rendering.

Now exit the container shell:

exit

Step 5: Desktop Integration on Fedora Host

To launch Cisco Packet Tracer directly from your Fedora GNOME Application menu, create a custom .desktop launcher entry on your host system.

Open your text editor on the Fedora host:

vi ~/.local/share/applications/packettracer.desktop

Paste the following configuration:

[Desktop Entry]
Name=Cisco Packet Tracer
Comment=Networking Simulation Tool
Exec=distrobox-enter -n ubuntu-pt -- packettracer
Terminal=false
Type=Application
Categories=Education;Network;
StartupNotify=true

Save the file and update the desktop launcher database:

update-desktop-database ~/.local/share/applications/

Testing the Installation

You can now launch Cisco Packet Tracer directly from your terminal:

distrobox-enter -n ubuntu-pt -- packettracer

Or simply search for Cisco Packet Tracer in your GNOME Super/Activities launcher!

item.title: Installing TeX Live 2025 on Fedora: A Minimalist User-Space Guide
item.description:
This guide consolidates the steps required to establish a professional-grade LaTeX environment into a single, clean workflow. Following this chronological order ensures that directories exist, dependencies are met, and the environment is correctly configured before the software attempts to utilize them.

By installing TeX Live in user-space (within ~/.local/opt), we adhere to a minimalist philosophy. This approach avoids cluttering the system root, removes the need for sudo during package management via tlmgr, and ensures you are using the most recent upstream binaries rather than potentially outdated distribution packages.

Pre-Installation: System Dependencies

Fedora's "minimal" Perl and X11 profiles often lack specific libraries required by the TeX Live installer and its graphical management tools. While we aim for a lean system, these Perl modules are essential for the installer's checksum verification and the tlmgr interface.

Install these requirements using dnf:

sudo dnf install perl-File-Find perl-File-Copy perl-Digest-MD5 perl-Tk perl-Term-ANSIColor xdotool

Create the Directory Structure

We will create a "user-space system" directory. Utilizing ~/.local/opt keeps your home directory organized while mimicking the Linux Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS).

mkdir -p ~/.local/bin

mkdir -p ~/.local/opt/texlive

Download and Launch the Installer

To avoid "checksum mismatch" errors common with unstable local mirrors, we will point the installer directly to the Comprehensive TeX Archive Network (CTAN) global repository.

cd ~/Downloads

wget http://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/tlnet/install-tl-unx.tar.gz

tar -xzf install-tl-unx.tar.gz

cd install-tl-*

Launch the installer using a reliable global mirror:

./install-tl -repository http://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/tlnet/

Installer Configuration (Text Menu)

Once the command-line interface menu appears, you must modify specific installation paths to point to your local directories:

  1. Directories (D): Change TEXDIR to: /home/porfirio/.local/opt/texlive/2025
  2. Options (O): * Toggle Paper Size to letter. * Toggle Create symlinks (L) to [X]. * Binaries: /home/porfirio/.local/bin * Manpages: /home/porfirio/.local/share/man * Info: /home/porfirio/.local/share/info
  3. Install (I): Start the process.

Note

The full installation can take approximately 3 hours depending on your connection. It is highly recommended to run this inside a tmux session to prevent the installation from terminating if your terminal session disconnects.

Post-Installation: Environment Setup

Fedora needs to be instructed where to find these new binaries. We will create a modular profile script in ~/.bashrc.d/ to keep our ~/.bashrc clean.

Create the configuration file:

vi ~/.bashrc.d/texlive.sh

Paste the following content into the file:

# TeX Live 2025 Path Configuration
TEX_BIN_PATH="/home/porfirio/.local/opt/texlive/2025/bin/x86_64-linux"

if [ -d "$TEX_BIN_PATH" ]; then
    # Prioritize TeX binaries and your local bin folder
    export PATH="$TEX_BIN_PATH:/home/porfirio/.local/bin:$PATH"
    export INFOPATH="/home/porfirio/.local/opt/texlive/2025/texmf-dist/doc/info:$INFOPATH"
    export MANPATH="/home/porfirio/.local/opt/texlive/2025/texmf-dist/doc/man:$MANPATH"
fi

Apply the changes to your current session:

source ~/.bashrc

Finalizing the Formats

With the paths set and Perl dependencies satisfied, manually execute the tasks that occasionally fail during the installer's finalization stage due to environment restrictions:

# Set default paper size
tlmgr paper letter

# Build the format files (Engines)
fmtutil-sys --all

Verification and Troubleshooting

To ensure your system is ready for document production, perform a "smoke test" by checking the binary location and compiling a dummy document.

Check the Binary Path

which pdflatex

This should return a path pointing to your ~/.local/bin/ or ~/.local/opt/ folder rather than /usr/bin/.

Compile a Test Document

echo "\documentclass{article}\begin{document}LaTeX 2025 is Live on Fedora!\end{document}" > test.tex

pdflatex test.tex

Summary of Locations

For future maintenance on your system, keep these paths in mind:

  • The System Root: ~/.local/opt/texlive/2025/
  • The Binaries/Symlinks: ~/.local/bin/
  • The Configuration: ~/.bashrc.d/texlive.sh
  • The Logs: ~/.local/opt/texlive/2025/texmf-var/web2c/fmtutil.log

You now have a professional-grade, upstream LaTeX installation that is completely independent of Fedora's system packages, making it easy to back up or migrate to a new machine in the future.
